bannedPatterns: NEVER put a solid/opaque background fill behind a word, a menu/stat VALUE, a price, a headline span, an eyebrow, a badge, or a label. A solid-fill box, pill, chip, or highlighter swatch dropped behind text reads as a CENSORSHIP / REDACTION BAR or a ransom-note tile — it is the single biggest amateur tell and an automatic fail. (The failing ARC board did this 8×: `.val{...color:#1a202c;background:#ffffff;border-radius:8px;padding:2px 10px}` made every value a white pill, and `.headline b{color:#1a202c;background:#fff;...border-radius:6px}` boxed the word 'Vision'.)

NEVER pick a dark ink text color and then 'rescue' its legibility with a solid box behind it. If your text would be unreadable as plain type on the field, you chose the WRONG text color — recolor the text (white / near-white / a bright on-brand accent), do not add a box. (Root cause of the ARC pills: `color:#1a202c` was unreadable on the red field, so a white box was bolted on.)

NEVER use `white-space:nowrap` on a row NAME cell or a row DESCRIPTION cell. nowrap on a fixed-width column guarantees long names ('Managed Print Services') ride over the dotted leader and the value. Names wrap/shrink via the flex contract; descriptions sit on their own line and may wrap. (ARC set both `.nm` and `.desc` to nowrap — the prompt's own anti-collision rule, violated.)

NEVER add `data-fit` to a row NAME or prose text — data-fit forces nowrap+shrink, re-introducing the overflow you are avoiding. data-fit is ONLY for short display text (wordmark, hero headline, big number/offer) and short fixed VALUES.

NEVER introduce a hue that is not in the supplied brand palette (no default Tailwind blue #3b82f6/#2563eb, no random complementary). If you find yourself writing a contrast patch for a clashing color (ARC literally shipped `/* Accessibility contrast tweaks for blue accents on red */` with `.tagBlue{color:#dbeafe}`), DELETE the clashing color instead of patching it. One brand color → build a monochromatic system of its tints/shades + one neutral.

NEVER place a saturated secondary hue directly on the saturated primary hue (blue-on-red, red-on-green, orange-on-blue) — these vibrate and lose edge definition at distance even when luminance contrast technically passes.

NEVER pair two interchangeable grotesques for display+body (Inter + Space Grotesk, Poppins + Montserrat, Sora + Inter-as-display). That reads as a default SaaS dashboard. The display face must be a characterful serif/slab/condensed/expressive cut. (ARC used Space Grotesk as its 'display' face AND for body — two grotesques, zero contrast of form.)

NEVER dim text with `opacity` to set its color — bake the final color in; opacity only ever makes contrast worse. (ARC's `.desc{...color:#ffe9e6;...opacity:.9}` is ~3.4:1 pink-on-red, illegible across a room.)
NEVER let two different content roles sit within ~15% of the same font-size (ARC: name 42px / value 40px). Differentiate roles by WEIGHT and COLOR when sizes must be close.

NEVER butt two flat color zones together at a hard seam with nothing bridging it, and NEVER paper over crowding with an edge-fade gradient (ARC's `.edgeFade` masked the missing gutter between content and the photo panel).

NEVER use a one-off 'nudge' pixel value or off-grid spacing (ARC's `margin:32px 0 28px 2px`). Every margin/padding/offset is an integer multiple of one 8px base unit, declared once as CSS custom properties.
NEVER use `box-decoration-break` (unsupported on Chromium-83 Taurus — renders as one ugly block) — and it is moot once headline emphasis is color-only.
typographyPriorityBlock: TYPOGRAPHY IS PRIORITY ONE. Before composition, color, or imagery, the text must be PERFECT: legible across a room, never overlapping, never boxed, never clashing. A board with flawless type and a plain layout beats a clever layout with broken type every time. If you can only get one thing right, get the type right.

THE #1 LAW — NO REDACTION BARS. NEVER place a solid/opaque background fill behind an individual word, a menu/stat VALUE, a price, a headline emphasis span, an eyebrow, a badge, or a label. A high-contrast solid block (especially white) behind text reads as a censorship/redaction bar or a ransom-note tile — the exact 'serial killer' look we are eliminating. This is an automatic fail. Count the filled boxes in your CSS before you output: anything other than AT MOST ONE CTA button (see below) means redesign.

EMPHASIZE WITH COLOR + WEIGHT, NEVER WITH A BOX. Make a value, price, or headline word stand out by recoloring it to the brand accent (or to white/near-white on a dark field) and/or increasing its weight to 700–800 — exactly like the exemplar's `.pr{color:<accent>}` and `.wordmark span{color:<accent>}`, which carry zero background. To stress one headline word use accent COLOR; if you want a marker feel use a low underline gradient covering only the lower third of the line (`background:linear-gradient(transparent 70%, <accent-at-35%-alpha> 70%)`), never a full opaque block behind the glyphs.

CONTRAST BY COLOR, NEVER BY INVERSION. On a dark or saturated field (strong red, navy, forest, plum) all text — including values and emphasis — uses pure white, ≥90% white, or a bright on-brand accent, read DIRECTLY on the field. Dark/near-black ink is ONLY for genuinely light surfaces (luminance > ~0.5). If the brand PRIMARY is light (pastel, yellow, mint), either darken the field for the text region or switch to ink text — never light text on a light field. If a chosen text color fails contrast, apply this fallback ladder and STOP at the first that passes — never invent a per-word box: (1) recolor the text white/near-black to suit the field; (2) deepen the underlying field (use the darker stop of the brand gradient under the text); (3) for text over a photo/busy area, lay a full-bounding-box semi-transparent palette scrim (rgba(0,0,0,.55)+ or a duotone) under the ENTIRE text block, sized to the text, never a thin edge fade.

CONTRAST FLOOR (signage, viewed across a room). Every glyph must clear, against the ACTUAL color directly behind it (test the WORST point of any gradient): display/headline/value ≥ 4.5:1 (target 7:1); body/caption/descriptor/eyebrow ≥ 7:1.

DISTANCE-LEGIBILITY SIZE FLOOR at 1920×1080 (scale proportionally for other canvases), and NEVER dim any of these with opacity: headline/wordmark ≥ 72px; section/value/number ≥ 34px; sub-headline ≥ 34px; body ≥ 28px; descriptor/caption/eyebrow ≥ 22px (eyebrow target 26px). Text below these tempts you to compensate with shouting boxes — size and color it correctly instead.

FONT PAIRING — CONTRAST OF FORM IS MANDATORY. Choose exactly TWO families: one CHARACTERFUL DISPLAY face (a serif, slab, high-contrast, or condensed cut with visible personality) for the wordmark/headline/item-names, and one CLEAN NEUTRAL face for body/descriptions/values. Never use the same family for both, and never pair two interchangeable grotesques. Pick from this menu by mood (display / body): Editorial-warm (cafe, bakery, boutique, worship) Fraunces / Inter; Luxury-serif (fine dining, salon, hotel, fashion) Cormorant Garamond or Playfair Display / Nunito Sans; Modern-editorial (corporate, agency, tech, AEC/print like ARC) Fraunces or Source Serif 4 / Inter; Bold-impact (gym, sports, bar, QSR, sale) Anton or Oswald / Barlow or Archivo; Friendly (school, kids, community) Fredoka or Poppins / Mulish; Clean-premium-minimal Sora / Inter. Reach for the DISPLAY face first; never default to grotesque-on-grotesque. When the display family has an optical-size axis (Fraunces, Source Serif 4) LOAD and USE the opsz axis tuned high for the hero (e.g. Fraunces:opsz,wght@9..144,800), and load the full weight range you use (a heavy 800/900 for the hero, 400–600 for body) so weight contrast is real.

TYPE SCALE — declare a confident ratio scale (~1.5–1.67 between adjacent tiers) and make every tier unmistakably distinct: DISPLAY (hero, ≥ 2.5× the largest content tier) · HEADING (item names / big numbers) · BODY (descriptions) · LABEL (eyebrow / section labels, smallest-but-tracked) · CAPTION (footer / fine print). Never let two roles sit within ~15% of the same size — differentiate by WEIGHT + COLOR.

TRACKING, CASING & LINE-HEIGHT LAW (apply to EVERY tier, never leave one at browser default): display/hero −0.02em to −0.04em (tighter as it grows past ~80px), line-height 0.9–0.95; eyebrow + section labels ALL-CAPS +0.18em to +0.34em; headings line-height 1.05–1.15; body/captions +0.01em, line-height 1.3–1.45; numeric values `font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums`. Set line-height explicitly on every multi-line block.

LEADER-ROW ANTI-COLLISION (mandatory, copy the exemplar verbatim) — a long name must NEVER ride on the value. NAME cell: `flex:0 1 auto;min-width:0;overflow-wrap:anywhere` and NEVER `white-space:nowrap`. LEADER: `flex:1 1 auto;min-width:12px`. VALUE: `flex:0 0 auto` (holds its width, never overlapped) with NO background, NO border, NO border-radius, NO padding-box — accent-colored tabular text only. Descriptions go on their own line beneath the name (`display:block`) and may wrap. Put badges/labels INLINE before the leader or on the description line — NEVER after the value.

SINGLE-MAX FILLED ELEMENT. The ONLY solid-fill container allowed on the whole board is AT MOST ONE call-to-action BUTTON, and it must use a contrasting ACCENT fill (never the same white used elsewhere), generous 14–20px padding, and read unmistakably as a button. If you use a filled CTA you may NOT also use a filled eyebrow pill or any filled value/headline box. An eyebrow/kicker is tracked uppercase text with a small leading accent TICK (`.eyebrow i`), not a pill. If a tag genuinely needs a container, make it an OUTLINE chip (1–2px accent border, transparent fill) or a translucent tint chip (rgba of a brand color at ~12–18%) — never an opaque swatch behind words.

PALETTE & SIGNATURE DISCIPLINE. Every color (fields, accents, gradients, scrims, photo duotone) comes from the supplied brand palette + tasteful neutrals; introduce no off-brand hue, and never collide two saturated hues. Commit to ONE accent applied as TEXT COLOR to every emphasized token (eyebrow tick, headline word, dividers, all values) and ONE border-radius token so the board reads as one coherent system. Pick ONE signature move (an accent tick echoed as a row marker, a duotone hero grade matching a color block, an oversized translucent brand initial behind the content) and repeat it 2–3 times — that recurrence is the difference between a designed piece and a template.

SELF-CHECK BEFORE OUTPUT — REDACTION + TYPE SCAN (do this every time): grep your own CSS for `background:#fff`, `background:#ffffff`, or any opaque `background:<color>` sitting behind a text element — if anything other than ONE accent CTA button has a solid fill, you built redaction bars: remove the fill and re-emphasize with color/weight/underline. Then confirm: no name/desc is `nowrap`; no value sits on a box; no body text < 22px or dimmed by opacity; no two saturated hues collide; no off-brand color; the display+body faces contrast in form; every value lines up on a shared right edge. If any check fails, fix it before returning.

contractAdditions: LAYOUT CONTRACT — ONE SPACING GRID: pick a single 8px base unit and make EVERY margin/padding/offset/gap/band-size an integer multiple of it (8/16/24/32/48/64/80/96). Declare tokens once as CSS custom properties (--pad, --gap-tight, --gap, --gap-section) and reuse them. No one-off 'nudge' pixels (no `margin:32px 0 28px 2px`).

LAYOUT CONTRACT — SAFE-AREA FRAME: apply ONE symmetric inset (--pad, ~72–96px) to the top, right, bottom AND left of every band; the footer's bottom margin MUST equal the side margin; no element touches a canvas edge.

LAYOUT CONTRACT — PHOTO-PANEL GUTTER: when a side photo/graphic panel of width P exists, set the content band's right edge to `calc(P + --gutter)` with --gutter ≥ 48px (ideally 64–80px) of REAL empty canvas — never let content butt the panel and never use an edge-fade gradient to hide crowding. State the relationship explicitly so it is intentional, not a magic number.

LAYOUT CONTRACT — RESERVED FOOTER CLEARANCE: the auto-fit script's reserved footer constant MUST equal the footer band's real footprint (band height + bottom margin) PLUS one section-clearance unit (≥48px), and the SAME number must be used in the CSS `bottom` math. (ARC's bug: JS `FOOT=150` while CSS pinned `bottom:46 + height:120 = 166`, so there was no guaranteed gap.)

LAYOUT CONTRACT — GRID-LOCKED COLUMNS: derive 2 columns from the spacing unit, not percentages — `columnWidth = calc((contentWidth − var(--gap-section)) / 2)`, gutter = one section token. Prefer ONE full-width wrapping column over a cramped 2-column split whenever long names would squeeze the leader below ~40px; legibility and aligned values beat column count.
LAYOUT CONTRACT — EVEN ROW RHYTHM: repeated rows share ONE row-gap token that reads visually equal whether or not a row has a description; the name→description gap is a separate tight token (4–8px).

QUALITY BAR — FOCAL HIERARCHY + INTENTIONAL ASYMMETRY: a uniform grid of identical rows reads as a spreadsheet. Establish one clear focal point and at least one deliberate asymmetry (feature one item/offer larger, or a 58/42 split instead of dead-even 50/50). Vary the type scale so the eye has an entry point.

QUALITY BAR — COMPOSE LAYERS WITH DEPTH: never two flat color zones at a hard seam. Build 2–3 relating layers (base field, a textured/duotone supporting layer, focal content on top) and let ONE element bridge any panel seam (logo chip, oversized brand initial, or the headline's last word overlapping the panel edge with clearance).

QUALITY BAR — BRAND-LITERATE COPY, NOT FILLER: generic-but-plausible copy ('Same Day', 'By Project', 'Bring Your Vision to Life') is a top 'AI-generated' tell. Echo the venue's actual positioning, named services, and voice from the reference; when a value/metric isn't given, prefer a real proof point (years, # of locations, a named capability) over an invented turnaround label. Never reduce a premium/specialist brand to a generic version of its category.

TAURUS AUDIT — add `box-decoration-break` to auditDesignerHtmlTaurus() warnings (unsupported on Chromium 83; renders headline emphasis spans as one wrong block — and is moot once emphasis is color-only).
rankedRisks: HIGHEST: the model treats 'no box behind text' as 'no box anywhere' and drops the one legitimate CTA button, OR over-corrects into low-contrast text it can't rescue (because the box crutch is gone). Mitigation: the rules pair the ban with an explicit positive alternative (color/weight/underline) AND the contrast fallback ladder AND a modeled accent CTA in the exemplar, so the model always has a sanctioned next move.

HIGH: the prompt is now very long; a smaller/cheaper model may ignore mid-prompt rules. Mitigation: TYPOGRAPHY-IS-PRIORITY-ONE block leads, the #1 LAW is stated first and repeated in the final self-check, and the exemplar MODELS every rule (models copy exemplars more reliably than they obey prose).

HIGH: the model keeps the redaction reflex because the EXEMPLAR never showed it the failure-vs-fix contrast. Mitigation: the exemplar's `.pr` and `.wordmark span` are now explicitly box-free with `background:none;border:0;border-radius:0;padding:0`, and a correct accent CTA is added — so the few-shot anchor demonstrates the boundary, not just describes it.

MEDIUM: monochromatic-palette rule produces flat boards when a brand truly has one color. Mitigation: rule pairs 'tints/shades + one neutral' with the signature-move + depth-layer requirements so a single-hue board still has hierarchy and craft.

MEDIUM: enforcing the contrast FLOOR with explicit ratios may push the model to add scrims it doesn't need on already-legible boards, adding visual noise. Mitigation: the fallback ladder is 'stop at the first that passes' and step 1 is recolor-not-scrim, so scrims are a last resort.

MEDIUM: 'no nowrap on names' + 'data-fit only on display' can conflict if the model puts data-fit on names anyway; ARC did exactly this kind of mis-targeting. Mitigation: an explicit banned-pattern line plus the verbatim flex contract make the correct target unambiguous.

LOW: the 8px-grid + safe-area-token rules are easy to state but easy for the model to approximate off-grid under layout pressure. Mitigation: CSS custom properties named in the contract make the grid a copy-paste, and the self-check doesn't gate on it — it's a polish rule, not a correctness rule, so a near-miss still ships a good board.

LOW: adding box-decoration-break to the Taurus audit is non-fatal/log-only, so it won't actually block a bad board — it only aids prompt tuning. Acceptable: emphasis is color-only after these edits, so the property should disappear from output anyway.
